newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weak on German sale plan.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weak on German sale plan.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended weaker on Thursday after German government sources confirmed plans to sell strategic reserves but news of a pipeline bombing in Colombia helped trim losses, dealers said.

August Brent closed 26 cents lower at $17.96 a barrel after dipping as low as $17.85 in the wake of Bonn's decision to raise 400 million marks ($230 million) this year from sales of government-controlled crude stocks.
Traders said the plan would release at least 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) at current prices -- the equivalent of a small North Sea field -- onto the market for the rest of the year.
"The German sale took the market lower early this afternoon but it steadied later with NYMEX," said a broker.
U.S. markets drew some support from the bombing of a key Colombian pipeline for the second time this week which forced Occidental Petroleum to halt production at its giant Cano Limon field.
Occidental said it was unable to pump any crude to the Caribbean loading terminal at Covenas until the 300,000 bpd pipeline has been repaired.
NYMEX gasoline was also helped by a small fire at Mobil Corp's refinery in Chalmette, Louisiana.
Earlier, IPE August gas oil closed $1.50 a tonne lower at $161.75, depressed by the losses on Brent.
The July contract expired at midday $1.25 down at $161.25. An IPE official said deliveries against the contract would total 1,223 lots or 122,300 tonnes, in line with market expectations.
